quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If you are riding in another vehicle's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Stay where you are so you don't surprise the driver.
Wave at the driver to get their attention.
Slow down to move out of the blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to move out of the blind spot.
questions.explanation: If you are in a vehicle's blind spot, speed up quickly or slow down to leave the spot.

questions.question: Unlike food and drinks, alcohol does not need to be digested. This means:

options.text: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts to affect the driver right away.
It takes a long time to feel the effects of alcohol.
Your body gets rid of alcohol very quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts to affect the driver right away.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested, so it enters the bloodstream quickly and reaches the brain within minutes. The body removes about one drink per hour.

questions.question: Which of these does not need to be checked regularly?
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your motorcycle's tires, controls, chains, sprockets, shock absorbers, fasteners, and brakes. Small problems on a motorcycle can be very dangerous.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. Drivers must follow these signs.

questions.question: During a pre-ride check, make sure that:

options.text: The brakes make a loud squeaking noise.
The brakes cause some friction with steering.
Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
Only the rear brake can hold the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Check each brake lever before every ride. Make sure it feels firm and holds the motorcycle when applied fully.

questions.question: What reduces the risk of head or neck injury in a crash?

options.text: Not allowing a passenger on the motorcycle

questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the best way to prevent head or neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: Which fabric gives motorcyclists the most protection?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants provide the best protection when riding.

questions.question: Use a turn signal:

options.text: When you plan to speed up.
Only when there is heavy traffic.

questions.explanation: Use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if you think no one else is around.

questions.question: If a driver is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Move to one side of your lane to share it with them.

questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them ahead of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up makes it more dangerous.

questions.question: Gloves can:

options.text: Make it hard to control a motorcycle and should not be worn.
Give you a better grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip on the handlebars and protect your hands in a crash.

questions.question: Which of the following is not protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Safe riders wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves.

questions.question: What is the proper body position on a motorcycle?

options.text: Sit forward enough so your arms bend slightly when holding the grips.
Sit as far back as possible and stretch to reach the grips.
Lean over the bike so your arms hold you up.
Keep your knees far from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit forward enough so your arms bend slightly when holding the grips.
questions.explanation: Sit forward enough so your arms bend slightly when holding the grips. This lets you reach and operate the controls easily and comfortably.

questions.question: If you ride on the right side of your lane while following a car, what happens?

options.text: You are in the best position to be seen.
The driver may not see you unless they use their side mirror.
The driver will know you are there.
You stop other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may not see you unless they use their side mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane behind a car so the driver sees you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check rearview mirrors much more than side mirrors, so this position makes you more visible.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What is the single most effective thing you can do to survive an accident?
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most important thing you can do to reduce your risk of injury or death in an accident.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to ride their motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Encourage them to use less-crowded roads.
Get friends to talk them out of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get friends to talk them out of riding.
questions.explanation: Never let someone ride if they have been drinking. Do everything you can to stop them. Get a group of friends to pressure them not to ride.

questions.question: When choosing clothes for riding, which is not a good choice?

options.text: A jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely
Boots or shoes that cover your ankles
A baseball cap to cover your hair

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap to cover your hair
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a jacket and long pants made of sturdy material, high sturdy boots that support your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: How often should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Inspect your motorcycle before every ride to prevent dangerous problems. Small issues on a motorcycle can be more serious than on a car.

questions.question: What footwear should you choose for riding?

options.text: Shoes with long laces that cannot be tucked in.

questions.explanation: Wear boots or shoes that are high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles. Heels should be short so they don't catch. Laces should be tucked in so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: What should your lane position do?

options.text: Keep your intentions hidden from other drivers.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Increase your ability to see and be seen.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
questions.explanation: Your lane position should help you see others and be seen by them. It should help you avoid wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. It should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Assume the passenger has ridden a motorcycle before.
Not assume they have experience and explain what to do.
Not explain anything since they are just a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume they have experience and explain what to do.
questions.explanation: Your passenger needs to know how to stay safe. Never assume they know what to do. Always give clear instructions before each ride.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, clothing:

options.text: Should be loose enough to flap in the wind.
Should not fully cover your arms or legs.
Should not include a jacket in warm weather.
Can protect you if you crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can protect you if you crash.
questions.explanation: The right clothing protects you in a crash. Always wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs, even when it is warm. Your clothing should fit snugly so it does not flap, but not so tight that it limits your movement.

questions.question: Motorcycles:

options.text: Do not have blind spots because they are small.
Have blind spots, but they are too small to worry about.
Have blind spots that you should check regularly.
Are too small to have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots that you should check regularly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks part of your normal scanning routine.

questions.question: To get the best protection, wear a helmet that:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly all the way around and have no visible damage.

questions.question: ____ can remove alcohol and its effects from your body.
questions.explanation: Only time reduces alcohol in your body. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers cannot lower your blood alcohol level or make you sober. They may keep you awake, but they do not change how much alcohol is in your system.
